about.title: Waterford Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Waterford is a small community in Stanislaus County, home to roughly 8,824 people. In 2025, the city's final collision record showed five injury crashes and eight people hurt, with no traffic deaths that year. That is welcome news, yet it does not soften the shock when a family here does lose someone suddenly — whether on Yosemite Boulevard, along Route 132, on F Street, at a worksite, or under someone else's care. California law gives certain relatives a way to seek accountability in civil court. A surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children come first; certain dependents and heirs may qualify after them. Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is far shorter when a government entity is responsible. Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to the financial support the person would have provided and the love, companionship, and guidance that cannot be replaced. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Waterford families, at no charge, with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Waterford Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then to certain dependents and heirs. An independent attorney can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early, not at the last minute
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, but it shrinks sharply if a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting connected promptly keeps those options open.

items.title: A civil path that stands on its own
items.desc: A wrongful death case proceeds separately from any criminal charges and can recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys take these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative died in a crash on Route 132 near Waterford. Does the state highway change anything?
items.answer: It can. Route 132 is a state-maintained road, and if a public entity's conduct or road condition is part of the claim, California requires a government claim to be filed on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. An attorney can evaluate whether a government entity is involved and act before that shorter window closes. The connection through LawProactive costs nothing.

items.question: We were never married. Can I still bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing is limited by statute. Registered domestic partners and children hold the first right to file, alongside a surviving spouse. Others may qualify only if they fit specific dependent or heir categories, so it is worth having an attorney review your particular relationship and circumstances rather than assuming either way.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, independent of any prosecution. The criminal case decides guilt and punishment, while the civil case addresses your family's losses such as funeral expenses, lost support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. Because the two-year deadline keeps running regardless, most families are better served by speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.
